append.text: **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:1) *Audíte, cæli* → *Escutai, ó céus*** (the row: *ouvi* refused, decision `audite`); the third person *áudiat terra* keeps *ouça*. The CNBB LH and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 also have *escutai*.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:2) *fluat ut ros elóquium meum* → *flua como o orvalho a minha palavra*** (D26's noun, v2): the v1 Latinist and stylist both asked for a noun parallel to *doctrína mea*; draft 1's clause *o que eu digo* is an option. Cost: *verba* one verse before is *palavras* too.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:4) *Date magnificéntiam Deo nostro* → *Dai magnificência ao nosso Deus*** — the row held against the v1 stylist (*grandeza*); DO's own antiphon for the canticle has *Date magnitúdinem*, which is *grandeza*'s word. **Listed as unknown by the ambiguity reader — the third time.**

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:7) *qui possédit te* (God, a person as object) → *que te adquiriu*** (v2, decision `possedit`): the v1 stylist and ambiguity reader both heard *que te possuiu* as sexual or demonic possession. The v2 Latinist (minor) asked *possuiu* back; held, and *possuiu* is the option. **For Gustavo: the row may need a person-as-object sub-row.**
**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:9) *Intérroga patrem tuum* → *Interroga o teu pai*** — the row held against the v1 stylist (*Pergunta ao*); the CNBB LH pairs *pergunta … interroga* in this verse.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:9; DO 32:12) *Jacob funículus hereditátis ejus* → *Jacó, a corda da sua herança*** — the row; the v1 Latinist (minor) asked *cordel* (the diminutive), refused (in Brazil *cordel* is chapbook verse first). The ambiguity reader heard a literal rope again. The CNBB LH has *a porção de sua herança*.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:10; DO 32:14) *custodívit quasi pupíllam óculi sui* → *e o guardou como a menina do seu olho*** (the singular, as 16:8); the v1 stylist asked for the idiom's plural *dos olhos*, refused.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:11; DO 32:16) the eagle *assúmpsit eum* → *o tomou*** (v2, the v1 Latinist: *recolher* leans to sheltering; MS1932, the CNBB LH). The row's *recolher* stays for the Lord taking in the helpless (26:10).

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:30, 36; DO 32:44, 32:53) *Dóminus conclúsit illos* → *o Senhor os encerrou*; *clausi* → *os encerrados*** — the row. The ambiguity reader heard *encerrou* as 'ended' and found *os encerrados* odd; held.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:34; DO 32:49) *signáta in thesáuris meis* → *seladas nos meus tesouros*** (v2): the v1 Latinist (treasury, not storeroom) and stylist (warehouse, bank) both asked *tesouros*; the ambiguity reader had heard *depósitos* rightly. **Against the row, by two readers — for Gustavo.**
**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:39; DO 32:57) *et non sit álius Deus præter me* → *e que não há outro Deus senão eu*** (215, 216). The CNBB Lectionary responsorial has *além de mim*, the option.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:22; DO 32:34) *terram cum gérmine suo* → *a terra com os seus brotos*** (plural for the Latin's collective singular; decision `germine`). No reader remarked beyond hearing crops.

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:6, 41; DO 32:6, 32:61) *Hǽccine reddis Dómino* → *É isto que pagas ao Senhor*; *Reddam ultiónem hóstibus meis* → *Pagarei a vingança aos meus adversários*** — the row held against the v1 stylist (*pagar a vingança* not a collocation; asked *Darei*).

**Canticle 226 (Deut 32:21; DO 32:31–32) *provocavérunt … irritavérunt … provocábo … irritábo*** — D27's local clause: both verbs in each line, God's answer measure for measure, so *provocar* for *provocáre* and *irritar* for *irritáre* (MS1932 the same). No reader remarked.

terms: | hostis (beside *inimícus*) | adversário (*para que os adversários deles não se ensoberbecessem*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:27, 41, 43; DO 32:40, 32:61, 32:65)**; *inimíci* and *hostes* meet in DO 32:40, so *hostes* takes *adversários*. The CNBB Lectionary responsorial has *dos adversários todos hei de me vingar* (32:41). MS1932 merges both into *inimigos*. |

| factor (God) | *que o fez* (*Abandonou a Deus, que o fez*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:15; DO 32:23)**; kept apart from *creátor → criador* (DO 32:27) as a clause on *fácere*. *seu autor* option; *feitor* is an estate foreman in Brazil. |

| recalcitráre | dar coices (*O amado engordou, e deu coices*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:15; DO 32:22)**; the fattened beast kicking. MS1932's *recalcitrou* is heard only as the figure ('resisted'), the option. No reader remarked; the stylist named the verse his best. |

| medúlla (trítici) | tutano (*com o tutano do trigo*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:14; DO 32:21)**; the Latin's image for the finest wheat (as *ádeps fruménti → gordura do trigo*, 80:17). The ambiguity reader did not take it as finest wheat and listed *tutano* unknown; *a flor do trigo* (MS1932's sense) is the option. |

| lactans (substantive, singular) | a criança de peito (*a criança de peito com o homem velho*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:25; DO 32:38)**, v2; draft 1 *o que mama* (8:3's plural *os que mamam*) was comic in the singular to the stylist and misparsed by the ambiguity reader. |

| cóndere (store up) | reservar (*Não estão estas coisas reservadas junto de mim*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:34; DO 32:49)**; *guardar* is *custodíre*'s, *esconder* *abscóndere*'s. No reader remarked. |

| sordes | imundície (*e não são filhos seus na imundície*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:5)**, v2: the Latin plural said in the singular (the v1 stylist). The loose construction of the Latin kept; *nas suas imundícies* (DRB) option. |

| circumdúcere | conduzir em volta (*Conduziu-o em volta, e o ensinou*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:10; DO 32:14)**, v2 (*ao redor* wanted a place, the stylist). The Latin's leading-about, against the LXX/Hebrew 'surrounded' (MS1932, CNBB LH *cercou-o*), the option. |
| concréscere | adensar-se (*Adense-se como a chuva a minha doutrina*) | open | **Canticle 226 (Deut 32:2)**, v2; draft 1 *Condense-se* was clinical to the stylist. *Cresça* (MS1932) option. |
